title: Scope: problem asks for explicit generators of I, solution gives an algorithm

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** 'Scope and honesty' paragraph (§1) and Corollary 5.3.

The problem requests, for EACH stratum, **generators of the relation ideal** $I$ — an explicit determination. Outside the purely cyclic (toric) sub-case, the solution's deliverable is '$I=\ker\Phi$, prime, finitely generated, computable by the elimination algorithm of §4', i.e. it characterizes $I$ but DEFERS explicit generators to running Buchberger's algorithm.

The honesty disclaimer ('no uniform finite list exists') is correct, but the published dihedral-invariant literature in which this problem is phrased gives EXPLICIT closed-form relations per stratum-type. Whether 'an algorithm that outputs generators' satisfies 'determine explicitly the ideal' is a genuine faithfulness concern.

**Fix:** derive and present the explicit closed-form dihedral invariants and their relations for the dihedral hyperelliptic families (e.g. genus 2,3,4,5), matching the literature, as the explicit ideal per stratum-type, with the algorithm presented as the uniform mechanism.
